body:
m1 - on "I HAVE NOT SEEN AN END-TO-END PATH FROM A REAL TRANSCRIPT TO AN ANSWERED RESEARCH QUESTION". The owner flagged that line, and I went to check it rather than agree with it. FIRST INSTALMENT: the fixture provenance, which is worse than "WOG is our only substantial fixture" and worse in a specific way.

THERE IS NO REAL HUMAN DATA IN THIS REPOSITORY. Not one transcript, not one participant recall. Every fixture is authored. Verified by reading their own docstrings, not inferred:

  WarOfTheGhostsModel.scala - 1,524 lines, and its docstring says "Hand-authored narrative
  acceptance fixture... it exists so the ontology, validators, renderer, and alignment contract can
  be exercised on one hard story BEFORE ANY AUTOMATIC ACQUISITION RUNS."

  WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite - "End-to-end alignment of the MANUAL RECALL PARAPHRASES against the
  HAND-MODELED STORY". So the recall side is authored too. Both sides of every alignment number we
  have quoted tonight are things we wrote.

  BirthdayInterview.scala - 146 lines, "A short SYNTHETIC Autobiographical-Interview transcript with
  INVENTED, neutral content."

I want to be precise about what this does and does not mean, because it would be easy to over-read.

IT DOES NOT INVALIDATE THE CORRECTNESS WORK. A ratio-of-sums is still right and a mean-of-ratios
still wrong on any data. The estimand migrations, the unforgeable types, the empty-guard rule - none
of that depended on the data being real.

IT DOES MEAN EVERY NUMBER WE HAVE QUOTED IS A PROPERTY OF OUR OWN PROSE. "specificity moves 4.8
points", "chronology rests on 30.5% of the route", "16 of 32 cells receive an imputed sensory score"
- I published all three today and every one is a measurement of text we composed. They are correct
statements about the code's behaviour on that text. They are not findings about recall.

AND IT EXPLAINS THE FIXTURE-DRIFT CLUSTER RATHER THAN LEAVING IT AS BAD LUCK. Three defects today
came from fixtures whose inputs were not in the pipeline's form - unstemmed lemmas, text without its
span's punctuation, point masses in a module about spread mass. That is not three coincidences. IT
IS THE PREDICTABLE CONSEQUENCE OF EVERY FIXTURE BEING HAND-WRITTEN AT THE CONSUMER. Data that came
through the pipeline cannot drift from the pipeline's form. Authored data drifts by default, and
only stops when someone checks - which is why all three were found by accident today rather than by
a mechanism.

So I would sharpen the chief's second barrier. It is not only that no researcher path has been
DEMONSTRATED. It is that the source side of alignment currently REQUIRES a researcher to hand-author
a fifteen-hundred-line narrative model per story, and nothing in the repo has ever produced one
automatically. That is the actual shape of the gap.

SECOND INSTALMENT to follow: I have a survey running on exactly where the automated path stops -
which steps run from raw text today, which require hand construction, and what the `acquire` module
actually does versus what its name promises. I will post the trace when it lands, and I will not
characterise acquire until I have read it.

One measurement I intend to take after that, because I think it changes the size of the problem: how
much of those 1,524 lines is IRREDUCIBLE, versus richness WOG has because it is an acceptance
fixture. If the minimum alignable StoryModel is eighty lines, the gap is a tooling problem. If it is
fifteen hundred, it is a research programme. Nobody has stated which, including me, and I am not
going to guess at it in a post about not guessing.
